mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by >2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises >0.3pp for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces earnings growth, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO remains below 98 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly for two months) and housing starts (HOUST) above 900K units for three months signals a demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.4% for two months AND HOUST > 900K for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS growth > 0.4% for two months and HOUST > 900K for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 3.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns: lower-than-expected monthly RSAFS growth (YoY < -0.2%) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS YoY growth < -0.2%.
